theory.intro: The **Medicare levy** is an extra tax that helps fund Australia's public health scheme. These exercises use a simplified model in which the levy is $2\%$ of taxable income unless another rate is stated, and is added to the income tax payable.
facts: For the simplified $2\%$ model, $\text{Medicare levy}=2\%\times\text{Taxable income}$.
$2\%$ as a decimal is $0.02$, so the levy is $0.02\times\text{Taxable income}$.
The levy is charged on taxable income, never on gross income, so subtract the allowable deductions first. Round calculated taxable income down to a whole dollar before calculating the levy.
Use the rate stated in the question when one is supplied. For example, the booklet's historical $1.5\%$ rate means multiplying taxable income by $0.015$.
In the simplified $2\%$ exercise model, a rise of $\$10\,000$ in taxable income adds $\$200$ to the levy. Both full taxable incomes are levied at the same rate.
steps: Multiply the taxable income by the levy rate

foundation.question_text:
A physiotherapist has a taxable income of $\$74\,300$.
Calculate her Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.

A hospital pharmacist has a taxable income of $\$88\,415$.
Calculate his Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.

An aged-care service manager has a taxable income of $\$196\,750$.
Calculate her Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.

A part-time carer has a taxable income of $\$21\,450$.
Calculate her Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.

A social worker has a gross income of $\$68\,900$ and allowable tax deductions of $\$1150$.
Calculate his Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Find the taxable income**
$\text{Taxable income}=68\,900-1150$
$=\$67\,750$
2. **Multiply the taxable income by the levy rate**
$\text{Medicare levy}=0.02\times67\,750$
$=\$1355.00$

foundation.question_text:
An occupational therapist earned a salary of $\$81\,240$ and $\$385$ in bank interest.
She claims union fees of $\$720$ and work equipment of $\$1105$.
Calculate her Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.
foundation.solution_text:
1. **Find the taxable income**
$\text{Taxable income}=(81\,240+385)-(720+1105)$
$=81\,625-1825$
$=\$79\,800$
2. **Multiply the taxable income by the levy rate**
$\text{Medicare levy}=0.02\times79\,800$
$=\$1596.00$

development.question_text:
A physiotherapist is paid $\$3145$ per fortnight and has allowable tax deductions of $\$1690$ for the year.
Calculate her Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.
development.solution_text:
1. **Find the taxable income**
$\text{Gross income}=3145\times26$
$=\$81\,770$
$\text{Taxable income}=81\,770-1690$
$=\$80\,080$
2. **Multiply the taxable income by the levy rate**
$\text{Medicare levy}=0.02\times80\,080$
$=\$1601.60$

mastery.question_text:
An allied health worker earns an annual salary of $\$138\,760$ and claims allowable deductions of $\$785.45$ for work-related travel, $\$426.80$ for computer depreciation and $\$198.65$ for professional membership.
Round the calculated taxable income down to a whole dollar, then calculate the Medicare levy to the nearest cent.
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Find the taxable income**
$\text{Deductions}=785.45+426.80+198.65$
$=\$1410.90$
$138\,760-1410.90=\$137\,349.10$
Rounded down, the taxable income is $\$137\,349$.
2. **Multiply the taxable income by the levy rate**
$\text{Medicare levy}=0.02\times137\,349$
$=\$2746.98$

mastery.question_text:
A pharmacist has a taxable income of $\$107\,300$.
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$18\,200 & \text{Nil} \\ \$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000 & 19\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$18\,200 \\ \$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000 & \$5092\text{ plus }32.5\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$45\,000 \\ \$120\,001\text{ to }\$180\,000 & \$29\,467\text{ plus }37\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$120\,000 \\ \$180\,001\text{ and over} & \$51\,667\text{ plus }45\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$180\,000 \end{array}$
Use the tax table to calculate her total tax payable, including the Medicare levy, to the nearest cent.

A social worker earns an annual salary of $\$156\,480$ and claims allowable deductions of $\$1268.75$ for work-related travel, $\$583.40$ for computer depreciation and $\$247.60$ for professional membership.
Round the calculated taxable income down to a whole dollar, then calculate the Medicare levy to the nearest cent.
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Find the taxable income**
$\text{Deductions}=1268.75+583.40+247.60$
$=\$2099.75$
$156\,480-2099.75=\$154\,380.25$
Rounded down, the taxable income is $\$154\,380$.
2. **Multiply the taxable income by the levy rate**
$\text{Medicare levy}=0.02\times154\,380$
$=\$3087.60$
